title: Fats Waller's character, selling tunes and writing "Squeeze Me"
summary: Fats sold tunes cheaply to others, and wrote Squeeze Me on a lonely New Year's Eve in Boston.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, the world knows Fats Waller and is familiar with him and his music, but I would like to ask a little about Fats in terms of his personality and how he fit in with his music, what type of guy he was.
Yes, one of the all-time greats.
He always seemed so happy, jolly.

Yes, he was, he was. Let me tell you about Fats. A lot of the tunes in those days that the famous composers had their names on, Fats Waller wrote and he'd sell them for $50.00 and $25.00 and $30.00. I don't want to call the names of some guys that I know that bought his tunes that they gave him $50.00 for. Some of the tunes that he wrote.
And they turned out to be very --
Hits, yes, yes. But then he began to write tunes that were of his origin and his own name. But Fats--
How long was he with you?

I was with -- yes. We were in Boston on a New Year's night -- New Year's Eve -- we'd been out of New York then about two months, on the road, and we're lonesome. If you've ever had experience in Boston, you know what a town it was in those days -- might have been from what it is now -- New

Year's and the whistles are blowing and the bells are ringing and here we're sitting in this dingy Back Bay front room of this brown front and Fats has got a piano. He say, "Maccey I'd like to be in New York, wouldn't you?" "I certainly would love to be in New York." He goes, "blim, blim, blue, bue," you know, "Squeeze Me?" "blim, blee, blum," that tune he wrote in New Year's Eve and we were sitting there wishing we were in New York. He wrote that tune right then and there.
Is that right? Now, what year are we talking about?
That's 192 -- later part of '22 or the first part of '23. The first part of '23, yeah.
He was still working with you?
